title: Microsoft Teams: users can report a security concern in meetings
summary: Hold: the reporting-destination command omits required argument values, and the alert-policy command creates policies rather than configuring the built-in reporting alerts. Microsoft also documents permitted changes to built-in alert policies, contrary to the briefing's note.

claims.claim: The printed Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy call configures the reporting destination using three parameters without argument values.
claims.quote:
Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy -Identity DefaultReportSubmissionPolicy `
    -ReportChatMessageEnabled $true `
    -ReportChatMessageToCustomizedAddressEnabled $true `
    -ReportChatMessageAddresses "securityadmin@contoso.com"
claims.fix: Replace the parameter-only call with a complete documented example, labelled 'Microsoft and reporting mailbox': Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy -Identity DefaultReportSubmissionPolicy -ReportChatMessageEnabled $true -ReportChatMessageToCustomizedAddressEnabled $true -ReportChatMessageAddresses "<reporting-mailbox>". Move '(Exchange Online PowerShell)' outside the code. For Microsoft-only, document the separate example including -EnableUserEmailNotification $true from https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/submissions-teams.

claims.claim: Defender alert policies are under Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Alert policy.

claims.claim: New-ProtectionAlert is the automation counterpart for governing the existing reported-meeting and reported-participant alert policies.
claims.quote: Use the New-ProtectionAlert cmdlet to create alert policies in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal and the Microsoft Defender portal.
claims.fix: Remove New-ProtectionAlert from this row: it creates a new policy, not configuration of the existing reported-call policies used by meeting reports. Set controls[4].api to null and explain that no supported command for changing these built-in policies was established. Do not substitute Set-ProtectionAlert: https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/set-protectionalert explicitly excludes default policies.

claims.claim: Manage Alerts is the role required to create and edit alert policies.
claims.quote: You have to be assigned the Manage Alerts role to create and edit alert policies.

claims.claim: The alert-policy page does not say built-in policies can be edited.
claims.quote: You can turn off these policies (or back on again), set up a list of recipients to send email notifications to, and set a daily notification limit. The other settings for these policies can't be edited.
claims.fix: Replace the last two sentences of the note with: 'Manage Alerts is required to create and edit alert policies. For built-in policies, Microsoft permits enabling/disabling, changing notification recipients and setting a daily notification limit; other settings cannot be edited.' Keep the existing UI path and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-xdr/alert-policies#default-alert-policies.
